One continuous fifteen-second live-action shot starting from the provided first frame, filmed by a completely stationary tripod camera. The three real actors, their faces, clothes, all props, the wooden ship deck, the staircase, the cabin with circular window and the stone theatre retain their exact appearance and positions from the first frame. Keep this one view throughout.
Celes is the blonde woman centered in the ivory gown and blue sash, holding the small coin on her open left palm. Setzer is the silver-haired man in the long black coat and gold waistcoat at right, holding playing cards in his right glove. Locke is the blue-bandana man at left with the wooden shield held low in his left hand and weapon sheathed. The ship is docked and remains still.

During the first four seconds Setzer acknowledges with a small nod and speaks exactly one short sentence in natural Brazilian Portuguese, with a mature male voice and synchronized lips: <d>[Portuguese] Combinado. Vamos levantar voo.</d> Celes and Locke listen with closed mouths. Setzer finishes speaking, gathers his cards into a stack and visibly puts the stack inside his coat. He withdraws his empty right glove.
Setzer then turns his whole body toward the already visible staircase behind him. He walks away from the camera, passing to the right of Celes with a clear gap between their clothes. Celes stays at her original mark beside Locke; both turn their heads to follow him. Setzer reaches the base of the existing stairs and places his right glove on the stair rail.
During the final part of the shot Setzer climbs the first three visible treads, one planted boot and weight transfer at a time. Each boot rests on solid wood before the trailing foot lifts. His coat trails his legs and his glove slides along the fixed rail. He settles on the third tread and glances back toward the two people on the lower deck. Celes gives a small nod and Locke shifts his weight, still holding the same shield. End with all three alive and responsive in their new arrangement. Continuous physical paths, exactly the original three bodies, steady lighting and rigid scenery.
Audio: the single Portuguese sentence from Setzer occurs only in the first four seconds; then every mouth stays closed and there is only quiet wind, fabric and card rustle, and separate wooden boot contacts. No other speech, singing or narration. This is one uninterrupted shot at normal speed, with the original camera fixed for the entire duration.
